passages.text: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God brought you out of the land of Egypt.
God is with you.
You may go out to war against your enemies.
You may see horses and chariots.
You may see an army larger than yours.
Do not be afraid of them.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֵצֵ֨א לַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה עַל־ אֹיְבֶ֗יךָ וְֽרָאִ֜יתָ ס֤וּס וָרֶ֙כֶב֙ עַ֚ם רַ֣ב מִמְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א תִירָ֖א מֵהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ הַמַּֽעַלְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and address the army, saying to them, “Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle with your enemies. Do not be fainthearted or afraid; do not be alarmed or terrified because of them.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel are about to go into battle against their enemies.
The priest comes forward to speak to the people.
The priest says, “Hear, O Israel.
Today you are going into battle against your enemies.
Do not let your hearts be weak.
Do not be afraid.
Do not panic.
Do not be terrified because of your enemies.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֕ה כְּקָֽרָבְכֶ֖ם אֶל־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִגַּ֥שׁ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְדִבֶּ֥ר אֶל־ הָעָֽם׃ וְאָמַ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּ֨ם קְרֵבִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־ אֹיְבֵיכֶ֑ם אַל־ יֵרַ֣ךְ לְבַבְכֶ֗ם אַל־ תִּֽירְא֧וּ וְאַֽל־ תַּחְפְּז֛וּ וְאַל־ תַּֽעַרְצ֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD goes with you.
The LORD fights for you.
The LORD fights against your enemies.
The LORD gives you victory.
passages.original: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם הַהֹלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּכֶ֑ם לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם עִם־ אֹיְבֵיכֶ֖ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Furthermore, the officers are to address the army, saying, “Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man dedicate it.
passages.sermon:
The officers speak to the people.
They say these words to the army.
They ask, “Has any man built a new house?
Has he not dedicated it yet?
Let that man go home.
He should return to his house.
If he does not return, he may die in battle.
Then another man would dedicate his house.”
passages.original: וְדִבְּר֣וּ הַשֹּֽׁטְרִים֮ אֶל־ הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ מִֽי־ הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֤ה בַֽיִת־ חָדָשׁ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֲנָכ֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־ יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יַחְנְכֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Has any man planted a vineyard and not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man enjoy its fruit.
passages.sermon:
God leads Israel.
God fights for Israel.
God gives Israel victory over their enemies.
The officers speak to the people.
They ask the men a question.
They say, “Has any man planted a vineyard?”
They ask, “Has he not begun to enjoy its fruit?”
If a man has planted a vineyard and not enjoyed its fruit, he must go home.
He must return to his house.
If he does not return, he may die in battle.
If he dies, another man will enjoy the fruit of his vineyard.
passages.original: וּמִֽי־ הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ נָטַ֥ע כֶּ֙רֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א חִלְּל֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־ יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יְחַלְּלֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Has any man become pledged to a woman and not married her? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man marry her.”
passages.sermon:
The officers speak to the people of Israel before battle.
They give instructions to the army.
They say, “Is there any man here who has promised to marry a woman, but has not yet married her?
Let that man go home now.
If he stays, he might die in the battle.
If he dies, another man may marry the woman he promised to marry.”
passages.original: וּמִֽי־ הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ אֵרַ֤שׂ אִשָּׁה֙ וְלֹ֣א לְקָחָ֔הּ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־ יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יִקָּחֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Then the officers shall speak further to the army, saying, “Is any man afraid or fainthearted? Let him return home, so that the hearts of his brothers will not melt like his own.”
passages.sermon:
The officers speak to the army.
They address all the soldiers.
They say, “Is any man afraid?
Is any man fainthearted?
Let that man go home.
He must not remain with the army.
If he stays, his fear may spread.
His brothers may become afraid like him.”
passages.original: וְיָסְפ֣וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים֮ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ הָעָם֒ וְאָמְר֗וּ מִי־ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַיָּרֵא֙ וְרַ֣ךְ הַלֵּבָ֔ב יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֛ס אֶת־ לְבַ֥ב אֶחָ֖יו כִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the officers have finished addressing the army, they are to appoint commanders to lead it.
passages.sermon:
The officers speak to the people.
They finish speaking.
The army needs leaders.
The officers appoint commanders.
The commanders stand at the front of the people.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּכַלֹּ֥ת הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ הָעָ֑ם וּפָֽקְד֛וּ שָׂרֵ֥י צְבָא֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: When you approach a city to fight against it, you are to make an offer of peace.
passages.sermon:
Moses speaks to the Israelites.
He gives them laws for war.
You come near a city.
You plan to fight against that city.
You must first offer peace to that city.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תִקְרַ֣ב אֶל־ עִ֔יר לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עָלֶ֑יהָ וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֵלֶ֖יהָ לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.
passages.sermon:
You approach a city to fight against it.
You offer peace to the city.
If the people in the city answer you with peace, they accept your offer.
If the people open their gates to you, they welcome you in.
All the people found in that city will become your forced laborers.
These people will serve you.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ אִם־ שָׁל֣וֹם תַּֽעַנְךָ֔ וּפָתְחָ֖ה לָ֑ךְ וְהָיָ֞ה כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם הַנִּמְצָא־ בָ֗הּ יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֛ לָמַ֖ס וַעֲבָדֽוּךָ׃

passages.text: But if they refuse to make peace with you and wage war against you, lay siege to that city.
passages.sermon: If the city does not make peace with you,\r\nand the city chooses to fight against you,\r\nthen you must lay siege to that city.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֤א תַשְׁלִים֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וְעָשְׂתָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְצַרְתָּ֖ עָלֶֽיהָּ׃

passages.text: When the LORD your God has delivered it into your hand, you must put every male to the sword.
passages.sermon: The LORD your God will give the city into your hand.\r\nYou must kill every male in the city with the sword.
passages.original: וּנְתָנָ֛הּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת־ כָּל־ זְכוּרָ֖הּ לְפִי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: But the women, children, livestock, and whatever else is in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder, and you shall use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God gives you victory over your enemies.
You may take the women in the city.
You may take the children in the city.
You may take the livestock in the city.
You may take everything else in the city.
You may take all the possessions of the city as plunder.
You may use the possessions of your enemies.
God gives you these possessions.
passages.original: רַ֣ק הַ֠נָּשִׁים וְהַטַּ֨ף וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה בָעִ֛יר כָּל־ שְׁלָלָ֖הּ תָּבֹ֣ז לָ֑ךְ וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֙ אֶת־ שְׁלַ֣ל אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel instructions for war.
God told Israel how to treat certain cities.
These cities are very far from Israel.
These cities do not belong to the nearby nations.
Israel must treat all these distant cities in the same way.
passages.original: כֵּ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ לְכָל־ הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים הָרְחֹקֹ֥ת מִמְּךָ֖ מְאֹ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ מֵעָרֵ֥י הַגּֽוֹיִם־ הָאֵ֖לֶּה הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: However, in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God gives you certain cities as your inheritance.
These cities belong to specific nations.
You must not let anything that breathes remain alive in these cities.
passages.original: רַ֗ק מֵעָרֵ֤י הָֽעַמִּים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּ֖ה כָּל־ נְשָׁמָֽה׃

passages.text: For you must devote them to complete destruction —the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that they cannot teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD your God gives you commands.
He commands you to destroy certain nations completely.
These nations are the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
You must destroy them as the LORD your God has told you.
You must do this so they cannot teach you their evil practices.
They do detestable things for their gods.
If you learn from them, you will sin against the LORD your God.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הַחֲרֵ֣ם תַּחֲרִימֵ֗ם הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָאֱמֹרִי֙ הַכְּנַעֲנִ֣י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ לְמַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ יְלַמְּד֤וּ אֶתְכֶם֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכֹל֙ תּֽוֹעֲבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ לֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַחֲטָאתֶ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: When you lay siege to a city for an extended time while fighting against it to capture it, you must not destroy its trees by putting an axe to them, because you can eat their fruit. You must not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?
passages.sermon:
When you attack a city for many days, you fight to capture it.
Do not destroy its trees.
Do not cut the trees with an axe.
You can eat the fruit from these trees.
Do not cut down the fruit trees.
The trees in the field are not people.
You must not treat the trees as enemies in the siege.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תָצ֣וּר אֶל־ עִיר֩ יָמִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים לְֽהִלָּחֵ֧ם עָלֶ֣יהָ לְתָפְשָׂ֗הּ לֹֽא־ תַשְׁחִ֤ית אֶת־ עֵצָהּ֙ לִנְדֹּ֤חַ עָלָיו֙ גַּרְזֶ֔ן כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ תֹאכֵ֔ל וְאֹת֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִכְרֹ֑ת כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ עֵ֣ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָבֹ֥א מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בַּמָּצֽוֹר׃

passages.text: But you may destroy the trees that you know do not produce fruit. Use them to build siege works against the city that is waging war against you, until it falls.
passages.sermon:
Some trees do not produce fruit.
You know which trees do not produce fruit.
You may destroy these trees.
You may cut down these trees.
Use these trees to build siege works.
Build siege works against the city that fights against you.
Continue until the city falls.
passages.original: רַ֞ק עֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־ תֵּדַ֗ע כִּֽי־ לֹא־ עֵ֤ץ מַאֲכָל֙ ה֔וּא אֹת֥וֹ תַשְׁחִ֖ית וְכָרָ֑תָּ וּבָנִ֣יתָ מָצ֗וֹר עַל־ הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הִ֨וא עֹשָׂ֧ה עִמְּךָ֛ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַ֥ד רִדְתָּֽהּ׃פ
